name: Orison Brushed Flannel Shirt
description:
Orison is a workwear-adjacent label that occupies the comfortable middle ground between functional and presentable — the kind of brand that outfitters stock alongside hiking gear and hardware stores carry alongside work gloves. The Brushed Flannel Shirt is a long-sleeve button-front in a medium-weight brushed flannel, cut generously through the shoulders and chest to allow movement without pulling. The plaid pattern runs in a traditional block check — a rotation of four colorways each season, always including a dark red/black and a navy/forest green. Two chest pockets with button flaps. A slightly curved hem that can be worn tucked or untucked.

This shirt has no technology in it. It is flannel. It is warm in the way flannel is warm — not aggressively, not technically, just reliably. People wear it open over a thermal layer on job sites, or buttoned up to the second button at a casual dinner, or thrown over a tank top on a cool morning before the temperature decides what it wants to be. It is the kind of shirt that appears in the background of every social tier from Tier 2 through Tier 3 without calling attention to itself. That is its entire point.
what_it_says: You don't overthink it. You put on a flannel shirt because it's a good flannel shirt.
worn_by: anyone who needs a reliable layer
story_hooks: A specific Orison flannel — dark red/black check, 2197 season — has appeared in three separate missing persons case files, worn by three different people, in three different locations across the corridor.
Orison's flannel fabric is woven by a single contracted mill that has just been purchased by a corponation that has no interest in continuing textile production.
Someone wearing an Orison flannel turns out to be significantly more dangerous than the shirt suggested — which was, in retrospect, the point.

physical_description.visual_profile: A classic long-sleeve button-front shirt with generous cut through shoulders and chest. Medium-weight brushed flannel creates a soft, slightly textured surface. Traditional block plaid pattern in muted, earthy tones. Relaxed silhouette suggests workwear heritage without aggression. Slightly curved hem allows styling versatility—tucked or loose.
physical_description.fit: Generously cut through shoulders and chest to permit unrestricted movement. Relaxed through the torso without being baggy. Sleeves have room for layering or augmentation interfaces. Slightly tapered at the waist with curved hem that hits mid-hip when worn untucked.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-weight brushed flannel—a natural-synthetic blend optimized for durability and thermal retention without active heating elements.
physical_description.texture: Soft brushed surface with subtle nap; tactile warmth. Light quilting effect from the plaid weave structure. Fabric has gentle give and recovery, feels lived-in immediately.
physical_description.color_scheme: Seasonal rotation: primary colorway in dark red and charcoal black with cream grid overlay; secondary in navy and forest green with white plaid. Both palettes suggest industrial utility and understated durability.
physical_description.closures: Full button front with wood-grain or matte resin buttons. Two button-flap chest pockets for tool storage or casual access.
distinctive_features: Traditional block plaid in four-color rotation
Two functional chest pockets with button flaps
Slightly curved hem for versatile styling
No visible tech integration or augmentation ports
Worn, well-maintained appearance expected after first wash
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 crossover. Affordable enough for working class; functional enough for corpo fieldwork. Ubiquitous across multiple social strata without signaling aspirational wealth or sub-grade scarcity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Workwear-adjacent aesthetic signals practical competence, outdoor familiarity, and refusal of corporate fashion theater. Worn by site engineers, logistics coordinators, independent contractors, and corpo middle-management on casual Fridays. Communicates reliability and self-sufficiency without political statement.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in appearance expected. Soft fading at seams and fold lines after first few months of wear. Possibly minor staining or patching by owner. Gains character through use rather than deteriorating.
